subject: music
title: Composing Stretch: Modulation, Development & Coherence
welcome_lead: Take your compositions to the next level with modulation, development techniques and a clear sense of unity.
meta_desc: GCSE Music Composing Adventure 3: stretch into modulation, development techniques, contrast and overall coherence.
final_note: Your compositions now sound polished, unified and confidently musical.

concepts.def: Changing key during a piece to add interest.
Varying a motif by changing pitch, rhythm or harmony.
Turning a motif upside-down (rising becomes falling).
Stretching a motif by making note values longer.
Shrinking a motif by making note values shorter.
A closing section that brings a piece to a clear ending.

walkthroughs.body_html:
The most common modulations are to the dominant (V) or the relative minor. To modulate smoothly, use a pivot chord — a chord that exists in both keys — then introduce notes from the new key.

Returning to the home key near the end gives a satisfying sense of arrival.

Strong compositions develop a small idea rather than constantly invent new ones. Inversion flips the contour upside-down. Augmentation doubles note lengths; diminution halves them.

You can also change the harmony beneath a motif, or move it to a different instrument — same idea, new colour.

Good pieces balance familiarity with surprise. Recurring motifs and key returns give unity. Contrasting sections (new texture, new key, new dynamic level) keep the listener engaged.

End with a clear coda — even a few bars referring back to your opening motif signals a confident close.

mcqs.q: Doubling all note values of a motif is called:
options: Diminution
Augmentation
Inversion
Modulation

mcqs.q: Which is the most common modulation destination from a major key?
options: The subdominant (IV)
The dominant (V)
The leading-note
A tritone away

mcqs.q: What is the function of the bridge in a pop song?
options: A piece six bars long.
It is the very first section.
It is the same as the chorus.
To provide contrast before the final chorus, often by changing melody, key, or texture.
Three sections: A, contrasting B, and a return to A (ABA).
Music in 3/4 time.
Three different sections (ABC).
It is the very first section.

mcqs.q: What does the time signature 6/8 indicate?
options: A piece six bars long.
It is the very first section.
Two beats per bar, each beat divided into three (compound duple).
Six beats per bar, all equal in stress.
